title: Trump and Musk Are Destroying a Priceless American Asset
gist: Fareed Zakaria argues that collapsing global trust in the US, symbolised by Musk's Starlink spat with India, is eroding the American nuclear umbrella and could push allies like South Korea and Saudi Arabia toward their own nuclear weapons.

insights.claim: Elon Musk's accusation that India is protecting Mukesh Ambani's Jio over Starlink backfired, drawing a nationalist demand to bar Starlink for national-security reasons.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Starlink's India launch faces political and security headwinds; Jio's own satellite service gains a protective advantage.
insights.locator: Elon Musk picked the wrong moment

insights.claim: Indian concern is that in a crisis with Pakistan its forces would depend on a US satellite system controlled by Trump and Musk, given Starlink's military version was restricted for Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Dependence on US-controlled infrastructure is becoming a sales obstacle for US tech abroad.

insights.claim: A Pew survey found China viewed more favorably than the US in 27 of 36 countries this year.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Soft-power erosion supports hedging and diversification away from US suppliers.

insights.claim: Favorable views of the US in South Korea fell from 77 percent in 2024 to 45 percent this year, and in Japan from 70 percent to about half.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Allies still dependent on Washington are losing confidence in it, raising political risk for alliance-linked assets.

insights.claim: Canada's Carney has rebuilt commercial ties with Beijing and moved closer to Europe, including European defense financing, earning very high approval ratings.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Reducing US dependence is politically rewarded, a trend favoring diversification trades.

insights.claim: The US nuclear umbrella, more than arms-control treaties, explains why only nine states have nuclear weapons despite Kennedy's 1963 warning of 15 to 20 by 1975.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: If the umbrella is seen as unreliable, proliferation incentives rise sharply.
insights.locator: The ultimate danger lies in nuclear weapons

insights.claim: An August survey found 65 percent of South Koreans support acquiring nuclear weapons, and a Post report said Saudi Arabia has not ruled them out.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Watch Seoul and Riyadh nuclear policy as tail risks for regional risk premia.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia signed a mutual-defense pact in August with Turkey and nuclear-armed Pakistan, while Gulf partners hit by Iranian attacks question whether hosting US bases makes them safer.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Gulf security alignment is diversifying away from the US.
insights.locator: Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates

insights.claim: Europeans are responding to doubts about US NATO commitments by raising defense spending, strengthening weapons industries, and France and Germany have created a joint group on nuclear deterrence.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Supports the European defense-spending and domestic arms industry theme.

insights.claim: Zakaria says the difference between asking allies to pay more and saying the US defense promise may be worthless is enormous; Trump may end up making allies build their own bombs.
insights.speaker: Fareed Zakaria
insights.so_what: Burden-sharing rhetoric has a proliferation cost.
insights.quote: Trump believes he is making America’s allies pay their own bills. He may end up making them build their own bombs.
